svg.title: Persistence, access, and natural use can dissociate
svg.desc: Three panels distinguish tagging, natural recruitment, tested contribution, and artificial access in mouse contextual fear conditioning. A shows training on Day 1 and separate tagging of selected dentate-gyrus or medial prefrontal populations. B compares c-Fos reactivation: tagged DG cells are preferentially reactivated on Day 2 but not Day 13, whereas tagged PFC cells show preferential reactivation on Day 13 but not Day 2. A separate inhibition row shows no detected freezing reduction on Day 2 and reduced freezing on Day 12 when tagged PFC cells are inhibited. A note identifies separate evidence for hippocampal support of PFC maturation. C shows direct activation of tagged DG cells in unconditioned Context B increasing freezing on both Day 5 and Day 15. The later population remains drawn and patterned. Assay dates and cohorts are distinguished, and freezing is identified as the measured response.

g.text: Separate tagging experiments; symbols are not cell counts.
B: Natural recruitment and tested contribution
Preferential: higher c-Fos-positive fraction in tagged than untagged cells.
Light ON compared with light OFF.
Separate experiment: hippocampal output supported later PFC maturation.
Separate activation assay; the same cohort was tested on Days 5 and 15.
Later tagged population: still accessible to stimulation
Freezing is the measured response; full remembered content was not tested.
